title: DevOps Engineering
subtitle: Build, deliver and run software through one automated pipeline
audience_line: Developers, system administrators and IT engineers moving into DevOps roles
overview: This programme follows a single change from a developer's commit to a monitored application running on AWS. Participants set up Git collaboration, build continuous integration and delivery pipelines with Jenkins and GitHub Actions, add automated tests, quality gates and versioned artifacts, provision the infrastructure with Terraform and configure servers with Ansible, then watch the result through metrics, logs and alerts. The same application is carried through every phase, almost every chapter ends with a lab, and the programme closes with a final project in which teams assemble the whole delivery chain and present it.

facts.label: Audience
facts.value: Developers, system administrators and IT engineers moving into DevOps roles

facts.label: Prerequisites
facts.value: Linux command line and Bash (course: Linux & Bash Scripting); Docker and Kubernetes basics (course: Docker & Kubernetes). This course builds on Docker & Kubernetes and does not repeat it.

facts.label: Duration
facts.value: 81 h: 72 h of chapters + 9 h buffer, in 27 sessions of 3 h

facts.label: Format
facts.value: Short lectures followed by guided labs; one application carried through every phase

facts.label: Lab environment
facts.value: One laptop per participant (16 GB RAM, Docker, VS Code) and an AWS sandbox account per participant, provided by the organiser

facts.label: Assessment
facts.value: A lab validated at the end of each phase and a final project presented to the group; certificate of completion for participants who complete both

facts.label: Outcome
facts.value: Participants can take an application from commit to production through an automated pipeline with tests, quality gates, versioned artifacts, infrastructure as code, and monitoring with alerts

phases.name: DevOps Culture & Collaboration
phases.focus: DevOps principles, Git and team workflows
phases.intro: DevOps starts with how a team works, then with how it shares code. This phase sets the vocabulary and metrics used for the rest of the programme and gives every participant a working command of Git and pull-request based collaboration.

chapters.title: DevOps Culture
chapters.content: CALMS, DORA software delivery metrics, Agile and Kanban, value stream mapping, where automation pays off

chapters.title: Git Fundamentals
chapters.content: How Git stores history (commits, trees, refs), init, clone, add, commit, log, diff, .gitignore, commit message conventions

chapters.title: Branching & Merging
chapters.content: Branch model, fast-forward and three-way merges, rebase, cherry-pick, conflict resolution

chapters.title: Remote Repositories & Pull Requests
chapters.content: fetch, pull, push, SSH vs HTTPS authentication, forks, origin and upstream, pull requests and code review

chapters.title: Team Workflow
chapters.content: GitFlow vs trunk-based development, branch protection rules, release tags, semantic versioning

phases.name: Continuous Integration & Delivery
phases.focus: Jenkins, automated tests, SonarQube, Nexus, deployment strategies, GitHub Actions
phases.intro: Participants build the same pipeline twice: on Jenkins, the most widespread self-hosted CI server, and on GitHub Actions. Tests, quality gates and an artifact repository make sure that only tested, versioned builds are deployed, and the phase ends with the release strategies that keep a deployment reversible.

chapters.title: Jenkins Foundations
chapters.content: Installation, plugins, security settings, controller and agents, job types

chapters.title: Triggers & Credentials
chapters.content: Webhooks, SCM polling, scheduled builds, credential types and their safe use

chapters.title: Jenkins Pipelines
chapters.content: Declarative Jenkinsfile, stages and steps, post actions, parameters, environment variables

chapters.title: Scaling Jenkins
chapters.content: Distributed agents, parallel stages, shared libraries for reusable pipeline code

chapters.title: Automated Testing in the Pipeline
chapters.content: Unit and integration test stages, JUnit reports, failing fast, disposable test environments with containers

chapters.title: Code Quality with SonarQube
chapters.content: Static analysis, coverage import, quality profiles, quality gates that stop the pipeline

chapters.title: Artifact Management with Nexus
chapters.content: Hosted, proxy and group repositories, Nexus as a Docker registry, versioning, cleanup policies, publishing from the pipeline

chapters.title: Deploying from Jenkins
chapters.content: Build, tag and push images to Nexus, deploy to Kubernetes with Helm, promotion between environments

chapters.title: Deployment Strategies & Rollback
chapters.content: Rolling, blue/green and canary releases, rollback, feature flags; push-based deployment vs GitOps (Argo CD, taught in Docker & Kubernetes)

chapters.title: GitHub Actions
chapters.content: Workflows, events, jobs and steps, hosted and self-hosted runners, matrix builds, caching

chapters.title: Secure Delivery with Actions
chapters.content: Secrets, environments and required reviewers, OIDC federation to AWS without long-lived keys, reusable workflows, deployment

phases.name: Infrastructure as Code
phases.focus: Terraform provisioning on AWS, Ansible configuration management
phases.intro: Infrastructure is described in code, reviewed like code and applied by the pipeline. Terraform creates the AWS environment for the course application; Ansible then configures the servers that run the team's tooling. Each tool ends with a project that the final project reuses.

chapters.title: Terraform Foundations
chapters.content: Providers, HCL, resources, data sources, dependency graph, init, plan and apply, fmt and validate

chapters.title: State & Variables
chapters.content: Variables and validation, outputs, state and the terraform state commands, S3 remote backend and locking, HCP Terraform

chapters.title: Modules & Environments
chapters.content: Writing and versioning modules, the Terraform Registry, workspaces, lifecycle rules, import and moved blocks, code organisation

chapters.title: Terraform Project
chapters.content: Provision the course environment on AWS: VPC, EKS cluster, RDS database and EC2 hosts for the tooling

chapters.title: Ansible Basics
chapters.content: Declarative vs imperative, configuration drift, architecture, static and AWS dynamic inventories, ad hoc commands

chapters.title: Playbooks
chapters.content: YAML, plays and tasks, core modules, handlers, conditionals, loops, idempotency

chapters.title: Variables, Templates & Vault
chapters.content: group_vars and host_vars, facts, Jinja2 templates and filters, Ansible Vault for secrets

chapters.title: Roles
chapters.content: Role structure, defaults, dependencies, Ansible Galaxy, designing reusable roles

chapters.title: Ansible Project
chapters.content: Configure the EC2 tool servers (Jenkins agents, SonarQube, Nexus) with roles, then rerun to prove idempotency

phases.name: Observability
phases.focus: Prometheus metrics and alerts, Grafana dashboards and Loki logs
phases.intro: A delivery chain is only finished when the team can see what runs in production. Participants instrument the course application, build dashboards from metrics and logs, and route alerts to the right people.

chapters.title: Metrics & Alerting with Prometheus
chapters.content: Metrics model, exporters, instrumenting the application with client libraries, PromQL, recording and alerting rules, Alertmanager routing

chapters.title: Dashboards & Logs with Grafana
chapters.content: Dashboards, Loki for logs, Grafana alert rules, contact points and notification policies, service level objectives

phases.name: Final Project
phases.focus: End-to-end delivery chain, presented to the group
phases.intro: Teams of two or three assemble everything from the programme into one working delivery chain for a provided application, then present it as they would to an engineering manager.

chapters.title: Brief & Design
chapters.content: Read the brief, draw the target architecture, split the work into a backlog

chapters.title: Build
chapters.content: Git workflow; CI with tests, quality gate and versioned artifacts; AWS infrastructure with Terraform; tool servers configured by Ansible; deployment to EKS with a rollout strategy

chapters.title: Monitor & Document
chapters.content: Metrics, logs, dashboards and alerts; README, architecture diagram, runbook

chapters.title: Demo & Review
chapters.content: Live demo of a change going from commit to production, then a rollback; questions and feedback

project.title: From Commit to Production
project.brief: A change pushed to Git is tested, analysed, versioned and deployed automatically to AWS infrastructure that the team provisioned in code. Its health is visible on dashboards with alerts, and a bad release can be rolled back.
project.stack: Git, GitHub, Jenkins or GitHub Actions, SonarQube, Nexus, Terraform, Ansible, Docker, Kubernetes (EKS), Helm, Prometheus, Grafana, Loki
project.deliverable: Repository with pipeline and infrastructure code, architecture diagram, runbook, live demo
